Abstract base class for all BehaviorTree nodes. Manages configuration, port IO with the blackboard, pre/post conditions, status changes, callbacks, and wake-up signaling. Derived nodes must implement tick() and halt(); type() returns the node category.

Concrete class defined in this header that derives from BT::TreeNode. It represents a leaf node in a behavior tree, forwarding construction to the TreeNode base with a name and NodeConfig. No additional members or behavior are introduced here; it primarily serves as a semantic base for leaf nodes. Destruction is defaulted and virtual via override. Details about TreeNode and NodeConfig are declared elsewhere.
Base class for all BehaviorTree action nodes. Derives from LeafNode and overrides type() to return ACTION. Intended to be the common base for different action execution strategies.
Synchronous action node that must not return RUNNING. It provides a default halt() that simply resets the status. executeTick() enforces non-running behavior, throwing if RUNNING is returned.
Convenience synchronous action that executes a user-provided callback (TickFunctor) when ticked. It does not support halting beyond the base SyncActionNode behavior.

Action node that executes tick logic on a separate thread. It exposes isHaltRequested() to allow cooperative cancellation, and maintains state for exception propagation, halt requests, thread handle, and synchronization.

Preferred base for asynchronous actions with explicit state transitions. Users implement onStart, onRunning, and onHalted. Provides cooperative halt handling and prevents overriding of tick() and halt() to ensure correct lifecycle.

Coroutine-based action node enabling cooperative suspension via setStatusRunningAndYield(). Uses a Pimpl to hide coroutine implementation details, provides a final executeTick(), and a customizable halt() with a recommended base call.

Condition node type for a behavior tree, derived from LeafNode. It resets its status on halt() and reports its NodeType as CONDITION. Constructor requires a name and NodeConfig. Destruction is defaulted. Actual behavior execution is inherited from LeafNode and not defined here.

Convenience condition node that invokes a user-provided callback (TickFunctor) on tick to compute NodeStatus. Requires name, functor, and NodeConfig at construction. Stores the functor and overrides tick() to call it.

Decorator node base class in the BehaviorTree.CPP framework. It is a TreeNode that manages a single child (child_node_) and overrides halt(), executeTick(), and type() to implement decorator semantics. It provides APIs to set and access the child and to halt or reset the child. Implementation details are not present in this header; behavior follows standard decorator patterns (modifying or gating the child node's execution).

The exact mechanics of child execution are implemented elsewhere; this header defines the interface and storage for the functor.

Concrete BehaviorTree class representing a control-flow node. Inherits from TreeNode (declared elsewhere) and owns a vector of child TreeNode pointers, providing APIs to add children, query children, halt individual/all children, and reset their states. Destructor is defaulted. Actual behavior is defined in the implementation file; details like scheduling and halt semantics derive from the BT library. NodeType reported is CONTROL.

Thread-safe key-value storage for BehaviorTree nodes to exchange typed data. Supports hierarchical parent blackboards, type-safe set/get, stamped retrieval, auto-remapping of keys, JSON export/import, and guarded access to values via AnyPtrLocked. Construct via static create(); destructor is virtual.

Internal record stored in Blackboard per key. Holds the current Any value, strong type information and converters, a per-entry mutex, a sequence id incremented on updates, and a timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch. Not constructed directly by users; created via Blackboard internals like createEntry/createEntryImpl or implicitly by set().

Base exception class for the BT namespace. Stores a composed error message and overrides what(). Accepts either a single string_view or a variadic list of arguments that are concatenated via StrCat. Intended to be thrown for behavior tree-related errors.
Exception type indicating logic/design errors (likely requiring code refactoring). Inherits from BehaviorTreeException and forwards constructors to compose the message.
Exception type for runtime-only problems related to data or conditions. Inherits from BehaviorTreeException and forwards constructors for message composition.

objects.description: Type alias for a buffer holding a serialized snapshot of a behavior tree’s node statuses. Each entry is a pair of (node_id, status_value), where node_id is a 16-bit identifier and status_value is an 8-bit code representing the node status. Intended for compact storage/transmission of tree state.

Function LibraryVersionString returns a pointer to a C string with the library version. This is not a user-defined type; no typedef or struct is defined here. No custom data type definition is present for this symbol. Note: included for completeness check — no type to document.

Abstract interface in namespace BT that parses behavior tree models (from file or text) and instantiates trees via a factory. It is non-copyable, movable, and defines pure-virtual methods to load sources, query registered tree names, instantiate a Tree given a root blackboard, and to clear internal state. This header only declares the interface; implementations must derive from Parser and implement all pure virtual methods.

Owns and executes one or more behavior tree subtrees. Manages lifecycle (initialize, halt), ticking policies, blackboards, and visitor traversal. Non-copyable, movable. Contains nested struct Subtree storing nodes and its blackboard.
A single subtree within a Tree. Holds the node list, its dedicated blackboard, instance name, and tree ID. Usually managed via std::shared_ptr through Subtree::Ptr and owned by BT::Tree::subtrees.

Concrete parser class for BehaviorTree.CPP XML. It derives from Parser (declared elsewhere) and can load trees from files or text, list registered trees, instantiate a Tree, and clear internal state. It uses the Pimpl idiom via a private nested struct PImpl managed by a unique_ptr to hide implementation details.

Singleton-like utility that manages JSON (nlohmann::json) serialization/deserialization for BehaviorTree.CPP value types. It stores converters for types and vectors of types, maps demangled type names to TypeInfo, and can translate between BT::Any values and JSON. Copy assignment is disabled to enforce single global instance (retrieved via get()). Template helpers register default or custom to_json/from_json functions.

objects.definition: using Entry = std::pair<BT::Any, BT::TypeInfo>;
objects.description: Alias within JsonExporter representing a serialized value: a pair of the value wrapped in BT::Any and its corresponding BT::TypeInfo. Useful as the payload for fromJson operations and for Blackboard entries.

objects.definition: using ExpectedEntry = nonstd::expected<Entry, std::string>;
objects.description: Alias within JsonExporter for an expected-like result of JSON deserialization, holding either an Entry on success or an error string on failure.

A RAII-like handle class (copy disabled) in namespace BT that loads and manages a process-local shared library at runtime, offering symbol lookup and platform-specific name helpers. It maintains a native library handle (_handle), the load path (_path), and a mutex for thread safety. The nested Flags enum controls dlopen() behavior on platforms that support it. Destruction does not auto-unload; callers should call unload() explicitly. Copy and assignment are disabled.

Nested enumeration within BT::SharedLibrary selecting loader linkage behavior: SHLIB_GLOBAL requests RTLD_GLOBAL; SHLIB_LOCAL requests RTLD_LOCAL on dlopen-based systems. Ignored on non-dlopen platforms.

RAII wrapper that owns a demangled C-string returned by BT::demangle_alloc and ensures it is freed via BT::demangle_free in the destructor. Non-copyable to avoid double-free; provides get() to access the underlying char const*.

Type-erased value container that stores and converts between numbers (int64_t, uint64_t, double), strings (via SafeAny::SimpleString), and arbitrary non-integral types. Tracks both the original type (type_index) and an internal casted storage type to enable safe conversions and validation. Provides casting, tryCast with error reporting, pointer access to stored type, and copyInto with preservation of destination storage type. Notes: integral inputs are stored as int64_t except uint64_t; float is stored as double; strings are wrapped in SafeAny::SimpleString. Conversions outside supported categories return errors. Behavior depends on external linb::any, SafeAny utilities, and nonstd::expected.

A namespace-scope static variable holding the sentinel type_index used by BT::Any to represent an undefined/empty original type. Pointer type shown for completeness; this is not a user-constructible type alias, just a variable of type std::type_index.

A small, read-only string class in namespace SafeAny that uses small-object optimization (SOO) to fit up to 15 bytes inline in a 16-byte object; larger strings allocate heap storage. Provides copy/move, comparison, size/data access, and conversion to std::string/std::string_view. Ownership is internal; destructor frees heap storage when not using SOO. Note: mutations are not supported; contents are set at construction/assignment.

Lightweight counting semaphore used internally by the timer queue to wake the worker thread. Supports notify(), timed waitUntil(), and manualUnlock() for interrupting waits without consuming the count.

Thread synchronization helper class that allows one or more waiting threads to be woken up by a signal, with timeout support. waitFor blocks up to the specified duration and returns true if a signal was received before timing out; it resets the internal ready_ flag after each wait. emitSignal sets the ready_ flag and notifies all waiters. Internally uses a mutex, condition_variable, and atomic flag. No custom construction/destruction beyond default; copy/move semantics are implicitly compiler-generated but copying such synchronization primitives is typically disabled or ill-formed, so treat instances as non-copyable and non-movable by convention. Thread-safe for the documented operations.

Concrete synchronous action node in the BehaviorTree.CPP framework that always returns NodeStatus::SUCCESS when ticked. It inherits from SyncActionNode, registers itself with ID "AlwaysSuccess" in the constructor, and overrides tick() to return success unconditionally. Useful as a minimal leaf that succeeds without side effects.

Concrete synchronous action node for BehaviorTree.CPP that unconditionally returns NodeStatus::FAILURE when ticked. Constructor forwards the node name to SyncActionNode with an empty ports list and sets the registration ID to "AlwaysFailure". Useful for testing and for explicit failure branches. Destruction/ownership follow SyncActionNode/Tree conventions; no additional resources are managed here.

A BehaviorTree.CPP synchronous action node that executes a parsed script. It loads/updates a cached script executor from the input port "code" and, on tick, invokes it with an environment built from the node's blackboard and enums. Returns SUCCESS after execution. Construction requires a node name and NodeConfig. Destruction/ownership follow the base SyncActionNode semantics.

BehaviorTree.CPP condition node that evaluates a scripting expression provided via input port "code". On each tick it (re)loads an executor when the script string changes, builds an Ast::Environment from the node config blackboard and enums, executes the script, and returns SUCCESS if the script result casts to true, otherwise FAILURE. It maintains the last script string and a compiled ScriptFunction executor. Construction sets the registration ID to "ScriptCondition".

BehaviorTree.CPP synchronous action node that writes a value into a blackboard entry. It either copies from another blackboard key if the input is a blackboard pointer (e.g., "{src}") or stores a literal string. It attempts type conversion when the destination entry already exists with a non-string type. Returns SUCCESS on write, FAILURE if the value resolves empty.

Concrete BehaviorTree.CPP synchronous action node that unsets (removes) a key from the blackboard and returns SUCCESS. It requires an input port named "key" of type std::string. Construction mirrors other SyncActionNode-derived nodes, taking a node name and NodeConfig; on construction it registers itself with ID "UnsetBlackboard". Tick retrieves the key input, throws RuntimeError if missing, then calls config().blackboard->unset(key) and returns SUCCESS.

A BehaviorTree.CPP stateful action node that sleeps for a specified duration before succeeding or proceeding. It uses an internal TimerQueue to schedule the wake-up, tracks the timer id, and guards state with an atomic flag and mutex. Destructor calls halt() to ensure any pending timer and running state are properly stopped. Exact success/failure semantics depend on onStart/onRunning implementations (not shown here).
direct_api_constructors: BT::SleepNode::SleepNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: Configuration struct for BT::TestNode. It defines the desired completion NodeStatus, optional scripts to run on success/failure/post-completion, an optional asynchronous delay to simulate async behavior, and an optional completion callback function. Used to parameterize TestNode behavior; ownership typically shared via std::shared_ptr<TestNodeConfig>.

A BehaviorTree.CPP StatefulActionNode used for testing. It can synchronously or asynchronously return a configured status, and optionally run success/failure/post scripts upon completion. Behavior is controlled by a TestNodeConfig supplied at construction (preferred via shared_ptr). Overrides onStart, onRunning, and onHalted, and uses an internal TimerQueue and script executors. Deprecated ctor takes TestNodeConfig by value; preferred ctor takes std::shared_ptr<TestNodeConfig>.
direct_api_constructors: BT::TestNode::TestNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config, TestNodeConfig)
BT::TestNode::TestNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config, std::shared_ptr<TestNodeConfig>)

objects.description: Concrete BehaviorTree.CPP synchronous action node that reports SUCCESS if the referenced blackboard entry was updated since the previous tick, otherwise FAILURE. It keeps internal state via a sequence counter and the entry key. Requires an input port named "entry" of type BT::Any. Construction requires a node name and NodeConfig; destruction uses base class semantics. Details of update detection are defined in the implementation (.cpp) and not present here.

A BehaviorTree.CPP control node that ticks its children in order, returning SUCCESS only if all children succeed, RUNNING if a child is running (without restarting earlier children), and FAILURE on the first failing child. It optionally supports asynchronous ticking when constructed with make_async=true. Internal state tracks the current child index and skipped/async flags. Specific semantics beyond comments depend on ControlNode and NodeStatus definitions in included headers.

A BehaviorTree.CPP control node that ticks its children in order and remembers progress between ticks. If a child returns RUNNING, previously ticked children are not re-ticked; on next tick the same child is ticked again. Returns SUCCESS when all children succeed, RUNNING when a child is running, and FAILURE immediately when a child fails. Maintains internal indices (current_child_idx_) and a skipped counter to manage iteration state. Construction requires a node name string; destruction is defaulted. Overrides halt() and tick() from ControlNode.

Composite control-node class in namespace BT implementing a Fallback (a.k.a. Selector) policy. It iterates over its children until one succeeds; returns FAILURE if all fail, RUNNING if a child is running. Maintains internal state for the current child index, count of skipped children, and whether ticking should be asynchronous. Inherits from ControlNode (declared elsewhere). Constructor requires a node name and optional asynchronous mode flag. Provides tick() and halt() overrides. Details of destruction/ownership follow ControlNode semantics; no special constructors are exposed beyond the provided one.
direct_api_constructors: BT::FallbackNode::FallbackNode(const std::string& name, bool make_asynch = false)

objects.description: Concrete BehaviorTree.CPP control node that ticks children from first to last, stopping on FAILURE, progressing on SUCCESS, and returning RUNNING if any child is RUNNING while halting remaining siblings. It is intended to have at most one asynchronous child; this constraint can be toggled via EnableException. Implements tick() and halt() overrides and keeps track of the currently running child with running_child_. Details of construction, destruction, and the base ControlNode are defined elsewhere.

BehaviorTree.CPP control node implementing a reactive fallback (selector) policy: ticks children in order until one returns SUCCESS; RUNNING or FAILURE causes ticking to continue to the next child. Returns FAILURE if all children fail. Designed to allow at most one asynchronous child; this can be enforced via EnableException(). Overrides tick() and halt().
Enumeration or type representing node execution status within BehaviorTree.CPP (e.g., SUCCESS, FAILURE, RUNNING). Only referenced in this header; it is not defined here.
Abstract base class for behavior tree control nodes. Only referenced as a base class; not defined in this header.

Control node that ticks all its children in the same cycle (concurrently in a cooperative sense, not in separate threads). It returns SUCCESS when the configured success threshold is reached, or FAILURE when the failure threshold is reached. Remaining running children are halted once a threshold is met. Thresholds can be provided via input ports "success_count" and "failure_count" with Python-like negative indexing semantics; -1 equals number of children. Fields track thresholds, completion set, and counters. Requires BehaviorTree.CPP types (ControlNode, NodeConfig, PortsList, InputPort, NodeStatus).
direct_api_constructors: BT::ParallelNode::ParallelNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: A BehaviorTree.CPP control node that ticks all of its children to completion within a single thread of execution (concurrently in the sense of the behavior tree scheduler, not via OS threads). Unlike a generic Parallel node that may early-stop based on success/failure counts, ParallelAllNode always allows all children to finish, but the overall node returns FAILURE if the number of child FAILURES exceeds the configurable threshold max_failures. It exposes halt(), tick(), getters/setters for the failure threshold, and tracks completed children and failure counts internally.

Concrete BehaviorTree.CPP control node implementing an if-then-else flow. It evaluates its first child (condition). If that child returns SUCCESS, it executes the second child; if it returns FAILURE, it executes the third child when present, otherwise the node itself returns FAILURE. The node is not reactive. It keeps an internal child index to manage execution across ticks.

Reactive control node that repeatedly evaluates its first child (the condition/statement) each tick. If the statement returns SUCCESS, it executes the second child; if it returns FAILURE, it executes the optional third child (else branch). When the active branch is RUNNING and the statement outcome changes, the currently running child is halted before switching to the other branch. Requires exactly 2 or 3 children. Inherits from ControlNode from BehaviorTree.CPP. Details such as internal state and exact halting semantics beyond the override are defined in the corresponding implementation file.

ControlNode-derived behavior tree control node that lets a user manually choose which child to tick via a TUI (ncurses). It maintains indices for the currently running child and the previously executed child. Exposes a static input port "repeat_last_selection" to optionally repeat the last chosen child. Lifecycle: constructed with name and NodeConfig, tick() drives selection, halt() stops execution. Destruction uses default base-class semantics.

A BehaviorTree.CPP decorator node that introduces a delay before ticking its single child. The delay duration is provided either via the constructor or through the input port "delay_msec" (milliseconds). While waiting it returns RUNNING; once the delay completes it forwards the child status. It internally uses a TimerQueue to schedule the delay and tracks state flags for start/completion/abort, protecting them with a mutex. Exact destruction/ownership semantics of members follow typical RAII; the destructor calls halt() to cancel timers and reset state.
direct_api_constructors: BT::DelayNode::DelayNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: A BehaviorTree.CPP decorator node that forces its overall status to be either RUNNING or FAILURE. It runs its single child and, when the child reaches a completed status (SUCCESS or FAILURE), it resets the child and returns FAILURE; otherwise it propagates RUNNING (or a skipped state as returned by the child). Intended to wrap a subtree to convert any terminal outcome into FAILURE, useful for control flow where success must be inhibited.

A BehaviorTree.CPP decorator node that forces its own status to SUCCESS whenever its child finishes (i.e., when the child reaches a completed status). While the child is still active, the node returns RUNNING (or propagates non-completed statuses such as RUNNING/IDLE depending on executeTick behavior). It derives from DecoratorNode and sets its registration ID to "ForceSuccess" for factory registration. The tick() implementation sets itself RUNNING, executes the child, and if the child has completed, resets the child and returns SUCCESS; otherwise it returns the child's current status. Ownership, lifecycle, and child management are handled by DecoratorNode (not defined here).

Enumeration type representing behavior tree node execution status (e.g., SUCCESS, FAILURE, RUNNING). It is referenced here to return values from tick() and compare against completion, but its definition is not present in this header. Details such as exact enumerators are unknown from this file.

Base class for decorator nodes in BehaviorTree.CPP, providing child handling (child_node_), executeTick(), resetChild(), setStatus(), setRegistrationID(), and isStatusCompleted(). Only referenced as a base; not defined in this header. Exact members and constructors are not included here.

A decorator node in the BehaviorTree.CPP framework that inverts the child node result: returns SUCCESS when the child returns FAILURE, returns FAILURE when the child returns SUCCESS, and propagates RUNNING unchanged. Constructed with a name identifying the node instance. Destruction is defaulted. Exact behavior of tick is declared here and defined elsewhere.
Enum or type representing node execution status used by BehaviorTree.CPP (e.g., SUCCESS, FAILURE, RUNNING). Only referenced here as a return type of tick(); no definition is provided in this header.

Decorator node class in the BehaviorTree.CPP framework that keeps returning RUNNING until its child fails. On child SUCCESS it resets the child and continues returning RUNNING; on child FAILURE it resets the child and returns FAILURE. It never returns SUCCESS. Requires an existing child node (managed by base DecoratorNode). Construction uses the public constructor with a node name; registration ID is set to "KeepRunningUntilFailure". Destruction/ownership follow DecoratorNode semantics.

Concrete DecoratorNode that repeats execution of its single child up to a configured number of successful cycles. The child is executed repeatedly: if it returns SUCCESS, the internal repeat_count_ increments; when it reaches num_cycles_ the node returns SUCCESS. If the child returns FAILURE at any iteration, the node returns FAILURE immediately. A special value (-1) for num_cycles enables infinite repetition until the child fails or the tree is halted. Ports: an input port "num_cycles" (NUM_CYCLES) can supply the limit at runtime. Construction/destruction semantics beyond standard C++ are not specified here; inherits lifecycle and threading rules from BT::DecoratorNode.
direct_api_constructors: BT::RepeatNode::RepeatNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: Decorator node that retries executing its single child up to a maximum number of attempts. Succeeds immediately if the child returns SUCCESS; on FAILURE it retries until max attempts or indefinitely if configured (via input port "num_attempts"). Inherits from DecoratorNode and overrides tick() and halt(). Constructors allow explicit attempt count or configuration-based initialization.
direct_api_constructors: BT::RetryNode::RetryNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: Deprecated alias class preserving the historical misspelling "RetryUntilSuccesful". It derives from RetryNode and provides identical behavior; constructors forward to RetryNode. Marked deprecated with guidance to use RetryUntilSuccessful instead.
direct_api_constructors: BT::RetryNodeTypo::RetryNodeTypo(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: Decorator node that ensures its single child is executed only once. After the child first returns SUCCESS or FAILURE, subsequent ticks either skip the node (return SKIPPED) or synchronously return the same terminal status forever, depending on the input port "then_skip" (default true). The class stores whether it already executed to completion and the terminal status observed. Requires BehaviorTree.CPP runtime types like DecoratorNode, NodeStatus, PortsList, and InputPort, which are defined elsewhere.

Synchronous decorator node that evaluates a scripted boolean precondition ('if' port). If the script evaluates to true, it ticks its single child; otherwise it returns the configured 'else' status (default FAILURE). Internally caches and reloads the parsed script executor when the 'if' string changes and ensures child reset when it reaches a terminal status.

BehaviorTree.CPP decorator node that encapsulates an entire subtree with its own BlackBoard. It allows explicit port remapping or automatic remapping via the _autoremap attribute. Provides a tick override and identifies itself as NodeType::SUBTREE. The class stores the selected subtree ID string and exposes getters/setters. Construction requires a name and NodeConfig; destruction is defaulted. Further semantics of PortsList, NodeStatus, NodeType, and DecoratorNode are defined elsewhere.
direct_api_constructors: BT::SubTreeNode::SubTreeNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: A decorator node that enforces a timeout on its single child. If the child remains RUNNING longer than the configured milliseconds, this node halts the child and returns FAILURE. The timeout can be provided in the constructor or via the input port "msec". Internally uses a TimerQueue to schedule the timeout and atomic flags to coordinate halting. Details of DecoratorNode, PortsList, InputPort, NodeConfig, and TimerQueue are external to this header.
direct_api_constructors: BT::TimeoutNode::TimeoutNode(const std::string& name, const NodeConfig& config)

objects.description: Decorator node that runs its child only when the referenced blackboard entry has a newer timestamp (sequence id) than the last observed one; otherwise it returns the configured NodeStatus if_not_updated_. It maintains internal state (sequence_id_, entry_key_, still_executing_child_) to detect updates across ticks.
Enumeration selecting how timestamps are reported by loggers: absolute time since epoch or relative time since the first observed event.

Abstract base class to log BehaviorTree node status transitions. On construction, it recursively subscribes to status changes from the given root node. Derived classes implement callback to receive timestamped transitions and flush to finalize output. Thread-safe dispatch via an internal mutex; can enable/disable logging and choose absolute or relative timestamps; can include or omit transitions to IDLE. Moveable, non-copyable.

Concrete logger class that prints BehaviorTree node status transitions to standard output. It derives from StatusChangeLogger and overrides flush and the status-change callback. The header declares the class; member function implementations are not provided here. Ownership and lifecycle are typical for a logger attached to a BT::Tree; further details depend on the base class. Exact semantics of Duration, TreeNode, and NodeStatus are not defined in this header.

Concrete logger class in namespace BT that writes a BehaviorTree to a .btlog file. It inherits from StatusChangeLogger and records node status transitions, writing asynchronously to minimize latency. Provides move semantics, disables copy. Owns a PImpl pointer for implementation hiding. Contains a nested Transition record describing a single status change entry. Requires a .btlog filepath per comment but enforcement details are in the implementation (not visible here).

Compact POD struct embedded in BT::FileLogger2 that represents a single status-change record: the event timestamp in microseconds since epoch, the unique node id within the tree, and the resulting NodeStatus encoded in 8 bits. Used when serializing the log stream.

Concrete logger class inside namespace BT that derives from StatusChangeLogger to record BehaviorTree status changes in a format suited for 'minitrace' JSON output. It keeps a previous time point to compute intervals between events. Construction requires a BT::Tree and an output filename for JSON. Full behavior depends on the base class and external types (Tree, Duration, TimePoint, TreeNode, NodeStatus) defined elsewhere.

Observer/logger that tracks per-node execution statistics within a BehaviorTree.CPP Tree. It listens to status changes (via StatusChangeLogger) and accumulates counts (success, failure, skipped, transitions) along with last status/result and timestamp. Provides lookup by node path or UID and exposes maps between paths and UIDs. Construction requires a BT::Tree reference; destruction is virtual via base. Details of StatusChangeLogger and Duration/NodeStatus/TreeNode come from included headers and are not defined here.

Per-node statistics record maintained by TreeObserver. Tracks last valid result (SUCCESS/FAILURE), current status (may be IDLE/SKIPPED), counters for transitions and outcomes, and the timestamp of the last update. Initialized with zeros/IDLE by default. Owned by TreeObserver as values in its _statistics map.

Logger that records BehaviorTree.CPP node status transitions and the XML tree into an on-disk SQLite database (.db3). It extends StatusChangeLogger, spawns a writer thread, buffers transitions, and writes into tables as per the documented SQL schema. It supports an optional ExtraCallback to append custom data per transition.
Opaque forward-declared SQLite C API connection handle. Only a pointer is stored; the complete definition is not present in this header.
Enumeration of all monitor request types exchanged with the BT executor and Groot. Underlying type is uint8_t; values map to single-character codes for protocol framing.

functions.name: BT::StatefulActionNode::isHaltRequested

functions.name: to_json
functions.signature: inline void to_json(nlohmann::json& js, const Type& p)
functions.description: Macro-generated serializer for a user-defined Type. When you expand BT_JSON_CONVERTER(Type, value) in the same namespace as Type, this function is defined and writes each declared field of p into js and adds a "__type" string with the name of Type. Intended to enable nlohmann::json ADL-based serialization for custom types used with BT.CPP.
requirements: This function exists only after invoking BT_JSON_CONVERTER(Type, value) for the concrete Type; otherwise it is not defined.
Must be declared in the same namespace as Type (or discoverable by ADL) so nlohmann::json can find it.
The AddField callback inside BT_JSON_CONVERTER must list all fields to serialize, and each field type must itself be serializable by nlohmann::json (i.e., js[name] = *val must be valid).
The output JSON will contain a "__type" field set to the literal type name (#Type); callers should not rely on this being absent.
js must be a valid nlohmann::json lvalue reference where object members can be assigned.
Thread-safety is not guaranteed; do not concurrently mutate the same js object from multiple threads.

functions.name: from_json
functions.signature: inline void from_json(const nlohmann::json& js, Type& p)
functions.description: Macro-generated deserializer for a user-defined Type. When BT_JSON_CONVERTER(Type, value) is expanded, this function is defined and reads each declared field from js into p using js.at(name).get_to(*v). It enables constructing or populating Type instances from JSON.
requirements: This function exists only after invoking BT_JSON_CONVERTER(Type, value) for the concrete Type; otherwise it is not defined.
Must be declared in the same namespace as Type (or discoverable by ADL) so nlohmann::json can find it.
The JSON object js must contain all field names specified in the _JsonTypeDefinition; js.at(name) will throw std::out_of_range if a field is missing.
Each JSON field must be convertible to the corresponding member type; nlohmann::json::get_to may throw nlohmann::json::type_error on mismatch.
The "__type" field, if present, is ignored by from_json; callers must not assume validation against it occurs.
p must be a valid reference to an initialized Type instance ready to receive field assignments.

functions.name: BT::demangle_alloc
functions.signature: inline char const* BT::demangle_alloc(char const* name) noexcept
functions.description: Allocates and returns a demangled C-string for a possibly-mangled C++ symbol name. When cxxabi is available, uses abi::__cxa_demangle to allocate a new buffer (malloc-allocated) holding the demangled name; on failure may return nullptr. When cxxabi is not available, returns the input pointer unchanged (no allocation). Typically used together with BT::demangle_free or via BT::scoped_demangled_name to ensure proper cleanup.
requirements: name must be a valid null-terminated C string; it may be a mangled C++ symbol name.
When cxxabi is available, the returned pointer, if non-null, points to a malloc-allocated buffer that must be freed with BT::demangle_free.
The function may return nullptr (e.g., demangling failure); callers must handle a null return.
When cxxabi is not available, the function returns the same pointer passed in and does not allocate; the caller must not attempt to free memory that it does not own.
Thread-safety of demangling is not guaranteed by this function; callers should ensure appropriate synchronization if required by their usage.

functions.name: BT::demangle_free
functions.signature: inline void BT::demangle_free(char const* name) noexcept
functions.description: Releases memory previously returned by BT::demangle_alloc when cxxabi is available. Internally calls std::free on the pointer. When cxxabi is not available, the function is a no-op and ignores the argument.
requirements: Only pass pointers previously returned by BT::demangle_alloc in environments where cxxabi is available; other pointers must not be freed with this function.
It is safe to pass nullptr; the function will do nothing in that case.
When cxxabi is not available, passing any pointer has no effect; the function does not take ownership of the argument.
Call this exactly once for each successful allocation returned by BT::demangle_alloc when cxxabi is available.

functions.name: BT::demangle
functions.description: Converts a (possibly mangled) C++ symbol name to a human-readable string and returns it as an std::string. This overload exists only when cxxabi is not available; in that configuration it simply returns the input name unchanged.
requirements: This overload is conditionally compiled and is only available when cxxabi is not available (HAS_CXXABI_H not defined).

name must be a valid null-terminated C string; it may be nullptr only if the surrounding code guarantees not to call this overload with nullptr (the implementation does not check for nullptr before constructing std::string).
No memory management requirements beyond standard std::string behavior.

functions.name: BT::demangle
functions.description: Returns a human-readable type name for the given std::type_index. Provides special-case readable names for several common types (std::string, std::string_view, and selected std::chrono durations). Otherwise attempts to demangle the compiler-provided name using scoped_demangled_name; if demangling fails, falls back to index.name().
requirements: index must reference a valid type_index obtained from a live std::type_info.
The returned std::string is independent of the lifetime of index.
Demangling may fail, in which case the result will be the implementation-specific name() string.
Thread-safety depends on underlying ABI demangler behavior; this function itself does not enforce synchronization.

functions.name: BT::scoped_demangled_name::get
functions.signature: inline char const* BT::scoped_demangled_name::get() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the demangled C-string managed by this RAII wrapper. The pointer may be null if demangling failed. The returned pointer remains valid only for the lifetime of the scoped_demangled_name instance.
requirements: The returned pointer becomes invalid immediately after the scoped_demangled_name object is destroyed; callers must not retain or use it beyond the object's lifetime.
The pointer returned may be nullptr; callers must handle that case.
No ownership is transferred; memory is freed automatically in the destructor via BT::demangle_free.

functions.name: BT::ValidCast
functions.signature:
template <typename SRC, typename TO>
bool BT::ValidCast(const SRC& val)
functions.description: Checks whether a value of type SRC can be safely converted to type TO and round-tripped back to SRC without loss. Performs range checks for integral targets and exact round-trip checks for integral-to-float conversions. Returns true if conversion is lossless by these criteria.
requirements: SRC and TO may be any types; additional safety checks apply only when both are arithmetic types.
For integral-to-floating conversions, the value must round-trip exactly (static_cast to TO then back to SRC must equal original).
For conversions to integral types, the source value must lie within [numeric_limits<TO>::lowest(), numeric_limits<TO>::max()].
Non-arithmetic types are compared via a round-trip static_cast to TO and back to SRC; callers should ensure such casts are valid in their context to avoid UB.

functions.name: BT::isCastingSafe
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool BT::isCastingSafe(const std::type_index& type, const T& val)
functions.description: Determines if casting the given value val (of type T) to the numeric type represented by type would be safe (lossless) according to ValidCast. Returns true if type equals typeid(T) or if ValidCast reports safe conversion to the specific supported target type (uint8_t/16/32/64, int8_t/16/32/64, float, double).
requirements: type must be one of: typeid(T), typeid(uint8_t), typeid(uint16_t), typeid(uint32_t), typeid(uint64_t), typeid(int8_t), typeid(int16_t), typeid(int32_t), typeid(int64_t), typeid(float), or typeid(double); otherwise the function returns false.
T may be any type; meaningful safety checks are performed when T is arithmetic.
Safety is determined by BT::ValidCast; callers relying on true must accept its losslessness criteria.

functions.description: Copies this Any’s value into dst, preserving dst’s internal storage type where possible. If dst is empty, it becomes an exact copy. If both are strings or have identical internal types, the value is copied directly. If both are numeric, converts to the numeric type currently stored in dst (int64_t, uint64_t, or double). Throws std::runtime_error if types are incompatible or conversion fails.

If both are strings, copy is allowed.

functions.name: BT::Any::tryCast
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
nonstd::expected<T, std::string> BT::Any::tryCast() const
functions.description: Attempts to convert the stored value to type T with safe, well-defined rules: direct cast if internal type matches; enums from numeric or from numeric-parsed strings; numeric-from-string via parsing; arithmetic conversions among numeric storage types; otherwise returns an error message. constexpr bool SafeAny::details::is_same()

functions.name: SafeAny::details::checkUpperLimit
functions.signature:
template <typename From, typename To>
inline void SafeAny::details::checkUpperLimit(const From& from)
functions.description: Throws std::runtime_error if the input value exceeds the maximum representable value of the destination type To. Intended as a guard before casting to narrower types.
requirements: From must be comparable with values of type From produced by static_cast<From>(std::numeric_limits<To>::max()).
To must be a type for which std::numeric_limits<To>::max() is defined (typically arithmetic types).
On failure, throws std::runtime_error with message "Value outside the max numerical limit."

functions.name: SafeAny::details::checkLowerLimit
functions.signature:
template <typename From, typename To>
inline void SafeAny::details::checkLowerLimit(const From& from)
functions.description: Guards lower-bound conversions. For To=bool, only accepts 0 or 1; otherwise throws. For other types, throws if input is below std::numeric_limits<To>::min(). Intended for safe narrowing conversions.
requirements: For To == bool, from must be exactly 0 or 1; other values cause std::runtime_error ("Implicit casting to bool is not allowed").
For non-bool To, To must have std::numeric_limits<To>::min() defined; throws if from < min.
From must be comparable to values of type From obtained from std::numeric_limits<To>::min().

functions.name: SafeAny::details::checkTruncation
functions.signature:
template <typename From, typename To>
inline void SafeAny::details::checkTruncation(const From& from)
functions.description: Validates that converting from From to To will not overflow or lose precision. Behavior depends on the category of From/To: (1) integer→floating-point: throws if the integer magnitude cannot be represented exactly in the target FP type; (2) floating-point→integer: throws if out of range or not an integer value; (3) other numeric conversions: throws if out of range or if round-trip cast changes the value.
requirements: From and To must be arithmetic types for which std::numeric_limits bounds and static_cast between From and To are well-defined.
Integer → floating-point: if the absolute value of from exceeds the exact representable range in the target FP type, throws std::runtime_error about precision loss.
Floating-point → integer: from must be within [lowest(To), max(To)] and an integer value (from == nearbyint(from)), else throws std::runtime_error ("Invalid floating point to integer conversion").

Other conversions: from must be within [lowest(To), max(To)] and must round-trip exactly (static_cast<From>(static_cast<To>(from)) == from); otherwise throws std::runtime_error ("Value outside numeric limits" or "Value truncated in conversion").

functions.name: SafeAny::details::convertNumber
functions.signature:
template <typename SRC, typename DST>
void SafeAny::details::convertNumber(const SRC& source, DST& target)
functions.description: Safely converts a numeric/string/enum value from SRC to DST with runtime checks to prevent overflow and precision loss. Handles integer↔integer, integer↔floating-point, floating↔floating, and conversions to bool with specific rules. On success, writes the converted value to target; on violation, throws std::runtime_error.
requirements: Compile-time: SRC and DST must satisfy is_convertible_type<SRC>() and is_convertible_type<DST>() (enforced via static_assert).
If SRC is signed and DST is unsigned, source must be >= 0; otherwise throws ("Value is negative and can't be converted to unsigned").
If SRC and DST are the same type, or SRC is float and DST is double, conversion is performed without additional checks.
If both SRC and DST are integers:
- If sizeof(SRC) == sizeof(DST) and SRC is unsigned while DST is signed, source must be <= numeric_limits<DST>::max(); otherwise throws.
- If sizeof(SRC) > sizeof(DST), source must be within [min(DST) when SRC is signed, max(DST)]; otherwise throws.
Conversion to bool (DST==bool) from integer/floating/enum is allowed without range checks (normal C++ truncation applies).
If exactly one of SRC or DST is floating-point, checkTruncation<SRC,DST>(source) must pass (no overflow/invalid/truncation) or a std::runtime_error is thrown.
On success, target receives static_cast<DST>(source).
Exceptions: throws std::runtime_error with descriptive messages when checks fail; callers should be prepared to catch std::runtime_error.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::SimpleString
functions.description: Constructs a SimpleString by copying the contents of a std::string. Uses small-object optimization (SOO) for lengths <= 15; otherwise allocates and stores a null-terminated copy.
requirements: str.data() must point to a valid buffer of length str.size().
If str.size() > 100*1024*1024, construction throws std::invalid_argument("size too large for a simple string").

Resulting internal buffer is null-terminated except when size()==15 (SOO at exact capacity), in which case the internal SOO buffer is not explicitly null-terminated; avoid APIs that require C-string termination (e.g., relational operators) for such strings.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns from another SimpleString by destroying current storage and recreating from other’s contents.
requirements: Self-assignment is not supported by this implementation; passing the same object as other leads to undefined behavior (the object destroys its own storage before reading from it). Callers must avoid self-assignment.
If other.size() > 100*1024*1024, assignment throws std::invalid_argument("size too large for a simple string").
On success, any previously obtained data() pointer or string_view becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::~SimpleString
functions.description: Destructor. Releases dynamically allocated storage (if any) and resets SOO metadata.
requirements: Must not be called more than once on the same instance (normal C++ object lifetime rules).
All outstanding string_views or data() pointers to this object become invalid immediately upon destruction.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::toStdString
functions.description: Returns a std::string containing a copy of the stored characters. Returns an empty std::string when size()==0.
requirements: None beyond a valid object instance. The returned std::string owns its memory independently of this object.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::toStdStringView
functions.description: Returns a std::string_view referencing the internal character buffer with the current size, or an empty view when size()==0.
requirements: The returned std::string_view does not own memory and becomes invalid if the SimpleString is destroyed, moved, or assigned.
Callers must not outlive the SimpleString when holding the view.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal character buffer. The memory is owned by this object and remains valid until the object is destroyed or modified by assignment/move.
requirements: The returned buffer is readable for size() bytes.

The buffer is guaranteed to be null-terminated except possibly when size()==15 (SOO exact capacity). Do not pass this pointer to C APIs that require a null-terminated string unless you have ensured termination (e.g., size()!=15).
Pointers obtained become invalid after destruction, assignment, or move of the object.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::size
functions.description: Returns the number of characters stored in the string.
requirements: None beyond a valid object instance. Result is in the range [0, 100*1024*1024].

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator==
functions.description: Compares for equality by length and then by the first N characters using strncmp, where N is this->size(). Does not require null-termination.
requirements: Both objects must be valid SimpleString instances.
Comparison reads exactly size() bytes from each object; callers must ensure objects are alive during comparison.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator!=
functions.description: Returns the logical negation of operator==. Uses length check and strncmp for comparison of up to N bytes.
requirements: Both objects must be valid SimpleString instances and alive during comparison.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator<=
functions.description: Lexicographical comparison using std::strcmp on the internal buffers. Requires both buffers to be null-terminated.
requirements: Both objects must be valid SimpleString instances and alive during comparison.

Both internal buffers must be null-terminated; this may not hold when either size()==15 (SOO at capacity). Using this operator in that case results in undefined behavior. Avoid using relational operators when size()==15.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator>=
functions.description: Lexicographical comparison using std::strcmp on the internal buffers. Requires both buffers to be null-terminated.
requirements: Both objects must be valid SimpleString instances and alive during comparison.

Both internal buffers must be null-terminated; this may not hold when either size()==15 (SOO at capacity). Using this operator in that case results in undefined behavior. Avoid using relational operators when size()==15.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator<
functions.description: Lexicographical comparison using std::strcmp on the internal buffers. Requires both buffers to be null-terminated.
requirements: Both objects must be valid SimpleString instances and alive during comparison.

Both internal buffers must be null-terminated; this may not hold when either size()==15 (SOO at capacity). Using this operator in that case results in undefined behavior. Avoid using relational operators when size()==15.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::operator>
functions.description: Lexicographical comparison using std::strcmp on the internal buffers. Requires both buffers to be null-terminated.
requirements: Both objects must be valid SimpleString instances and alive during comparison.

Both internal buffers must be null-terminated; this may not hold when either size()==15 (SOO at capacity). Using this operator in that case results in undefined behavior. Avoid using relational operators when size()==15.

functions.name: SafeAny::SimpleString::isSOO
functions.description: Returns true if the string is stored in the small-object-optimized inline buffer (length <= 15), false if stored in a dynamically allocated buffer.
requirements: None beyond a valid object instance.

functions.name: BT::StrCat
functions.description: Create and return an empty std::string. Intended as the zero-argument baseline overload of the concatenation utility.
requirements: No arguments required.
Callers should expect a new empty std::string to be returned.
May allocate minimally (implementation-defined); no other side effects.

functions.name: BT::StrCat
functions.description: Return a new std::string containing the characters of a. Fast path for constructing a std::string from a single string-like input.
requirements: Argument a must refer to a valid memory range for the duration of the call.
a may be any type implicitly convertible to std::string_view (e.g., const char*, std::string, std::string_view).
May throw on allocation or append (e.g., std::bad_alloc).

functions.name: BT::StrCat
functions.signature: std::string BT::StrCat(const std::string_view& a, const std::string_view& b)
functions.description: Return a new std::string formed by concatenating a followed by b with no delimiter.
requirements: Arguments a and b must each refer to valid memory for the duration of the call.
a and b may be any types implicitly convertible to std::string_view.
Total size (a.size()+b.size()) must fit within std::string's size limits; otherwise construction/append may throw.

functions.name: BT::StrCat
functions.signature: std::string BT::StrCat(const std::string_view& a, const std::string_view& b, const std::string_view& c)
functions.description: Return a new std::string formed by concatenating a, b, and c with no delimiter. Uses a single pre-reserve for performance.
requirements: Arguments a, b, and c must refer to valid memory for the duration of the call.
Each argument may be any type implicitly convertible to std::string_view.
Total concatenated size must fit within std::string limits; operations may throw on allocation.

functions.name: BT::StrAppend
functions.signature: void BT::StrAppend(std::string* destination, const std::string_view& a)
functions.description: Append a to the end of *destination with no delimiter. Optimized path for a single piece.
requirements: destination must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized std::string.
a must refer to valid memory for the duration of the call and may be any type implicitly convertible to std::string_view.
May reallocate destination’s internal buffer; may throw on allocation/append.

functions.name: BT::StrAppend
functions.signature: void BT::StrAppend(std::string* destination, const std::string_view& a, const std::string_view& b)
functions.description: Append a then b to *destination with no delimiter. Performs a single capacity reservation sized for both pieces.
requirements: destination must be non-null and point to a valid std::string.
a and b must be valid for the duration of the call and convertible to std::string_view if not already.

functions.name: BT::StrAppend
functions.signature: void BT::StrAppend(std::string* destination, const std::string_view& a, const std::string_view& b, const std::string_view& c)
functions.description: Append a, b, and c to *destination with no delimiter. Reserves cumulative size before appending for efficiency.

functions.name: BT::StrAppend
functions.signature: template <typename... AV> void BT::StrAppend(std::string* destination, const std::string_view& a, const std::string_view& b, const std::string_view& c, const std::string_view& d, const AV&... args)

functions.name: BT::details::Semaphore::Semaphore
functions.description: Constructs a lightweight semaphore initialized with the given count. Use to coordinate threads; each notify() increments the count, and waitUntil(...) will decrement the count when it successfully acquires.
requirements: May be constructed with any unsigned count; a nonzero count allows up to that many successful waits without blocking.
Object must remain alive while other threads call notify(), waitUntil(...), or manualUnlock().

functions.name: BT::details::Semaphore::notify
functions.description: Signals the semaphore by incrementing its internal count and waking one waiting thread, if any.
requirements: The semaphore object must be valid and not destroyed when called.
Can be called from any thread; no other explicit restrictions.

functions.name: BT::details::Semaphore::waitUntil
functions.signature: template <class Clock, class Duration> bool BT::details::Semaphore::waitUntil(const std::chrono::time_point<Clock, Duration>& point)
functions.description: Blocks until either the semaphore is signaled (count > 0) or until the specified absolute time_point is reached, or until a manualUnlock() occurs. On success, it consumes one count (if any) and returns true; if the timeout expires without a signal it returns false. If awakened via manualUnlock(), returns true without decrementing the count.
requirements: Must be called with a valid std::chrono::time_point from any clock/duration types.
Caller should handle both return values: true (signaled or manually unlocked) and false (timeout).
The semaphore object must remain valid for the duration of the wait.

functions.name: BT::details::Semaphore::manualUnlock
functions.description: Manually wakes one waiter without consuming the semaphore count. Used to break a wait without producing a count-based signal.
requirements: Semaphore must be valid while calling manualUnlock().
Caller should expect the next waiter to return true from waitUntil(...) even if the count is zero.

functions.name: BT::TimerQueue::TimerQueue
functions.description: Constructs a timer queue and starts a dedicated worker thread to manage and execute scheduled handlers. Handlers will always execute on this worker thread.
requirements: The TimerQueue object must outlive any scheduled handlers; destroying the queue cancels all timers and joins the worker thread.
Handlers executed by this queue must be safe to run on the queue’s worker thread.

functions.name: BT::TimerQueue::~TimerQueue
functions.description: Stops the timer queue: requests shutdown, cancels all timers (invoking their handlers with aborted=true), and joins the worker thread.
requirements: Must not be invoked while another thread is concurrently destroying the same object.
Handlers may be invoked during destruction with aborted=true; caller-supplied handlers must tolerate being called during shutdown.

functions.name: BT::TimerQueue::add
functions.signature: template <typename _Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock, typename _Duration = std::chrono::steady_clock::duration> uint64_t BT::TimerQueue<_Clock, _Duration>::add(std::chrono::milliseconds milliseconds, std::function<void(bool)> handler)
functions.description: Schedules a handler to run after the specified delay. Returns a timer ID that can be used to cancel the timer. The handler is invoked exactly once on the queue’s worker thread; if the timer is canceled before firing, the handler is still invoked with its bool parameter set to true (aborted).
requirements: Handler must be a valid callable matching void(bool).
The TimerQueue instance must remain alive until the handler runs or the timer is canceled.
No ordering of handler execution is guaranteed relative to other timers.

functions.name: BT::TimerQueue::cancel
functions.signature: template <typename _Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock, typename _Duration = std::chrono::steady_clock::duration> size_t BT::TimerQueue<_Clock, _Duration>::cancel(uint64_t id)
functions.description: Attempts to cancel the timer with the given ID. If successful, schedules its handler for immediate execution on the worker thread with aborted=true and returns 1. Returns 0 if the timer has already fired or the ID is invalid.
requirements: id should be an ID previously returned by add(...); otherwise the function returns 0.
Caller must be prepared for the handler to execute immediately after cancellation request (on the worker thread).

functions.name: BT::TimerQueue::cancelAll
functions.signature: template <typename _Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock, typename _Duration = std::chrono::steady_clock::duration> size_t BT::TimerQueue<_Clock, _Duration>::cancelAll()
functions.description: Cancels all pending timers by marking them for immediate execution with aborted=true. Returns the number of timers present at the time of cancellation request.
requirements: May be called at any time; handlers will execute on the worker thread with aborted=true.
Caller should not assume any particular execution order of the canceled handlers.

functions.name: BT::TimerQueue::Queue::getContainer
functions.signature: template <typename _Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock, typename _Duration = std::chrono::steady_clock::duration> std::vector<typename BT::TimerQueue<_Clock, _Duration>::WorkItem>& BT::TimerQueue<_Clock, _Duration>::Queue::getContainer()
functions.description: Provides direct access to the underlying container of the priority queue used by TimerQueue. Intended for internal use to iterate and adjust items without breaking the heap property.
requirements: Mutating the returned container can violate the priority_queue invariants; caller must preserve heap integrity if modifying contents.
Intended for internal use within TimerQueue; external use risks undefined behavior of the queue’s ordering.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::LockedPtr
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty LockedPtr. No object or mutex is associated; no lock is taken. Use operator bool() or get() to check for an associated object before use.
requirements: No requirements; the resulting instance has ref_ == nullptr and mutex_ == nullptr.

Caller must not attempt to dereference through operator->() or call assign() unless an object has later been associated (not possible with this interface); effectively this default-constructed instance is only useful as a placeholder.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::~LockedPtr
functions.description: Destructor. If a mutex is associated, it calls unlock() on it. This pairs with the constructor that locks the mutex, providing RAII unlocking at scope exit.
requirements: If the caller has manually called unlock() on the associated mutex via this object, they must ensure the mutex is re-locked before destruction; otherwise the destructor will attempt to unlock an unlocked mutex, which is undefined behavior.
The associated std::mutex* (if any) must still be valid when the destructor runs.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::operator=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
BT::LockedPtr<T>& BT::LockedPtr<T>::operator=(const BT::LockedPtr<T>&) = delete
functions.description: Copy assignment operator is deleted. LockedPtr cannot be copy-assigned to avoid multiple owners of the same lock and double-unlocking.
requirements: This operator cannot be used; attempting to copy-assign will not compile.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::operator bool
functions.description: Boolean conversion that returns true if the LockedPtr currently references a non-null object pointer, false otherwise. Useful for guard checks before access.
requirements: No special requirements; safe to call even if default-constructed.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::lock
functions.description: Locks the associated mutex if present. Normally unnecessary because the (T*, std::mutex*) constructor already locks the mutex; provided to allow manual unlock/re-lock sequences while the object is in scope.
requirements: If no mutex is associated (mutex_ == nullptr), this is a no-op.
Caller must not cause deadlocks (do not call if the mutex is already locked by the same thread for a non-recursive mutex).
If the caller previously called unlock(), they must ensure proper pairing so that the destructor does not unlock an already-unlocked mutex.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::unlock
functions.description: Unlocks the associated mutex if present. Use with care; the destructor will also call unlock() if a mutex is set.
requirements: If no mutex is associated (mutex_ == nullptr), this is a no-op.
Unlocking an unlocked std::mutex is undefined behavior; the caller must ensure the mutex is currently locked before calling unlock().

Because the destructor will unconditionally unlock if a mutex is present, the caller should re-lock the mutex (via lock()) before destruction, or avoid calling unlock() unless they manage the lock state carefully.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::get
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const T* BT::LockedPtr<T>::get() const
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer to the referenced object (which may be null). Does not modify locking state.
requirements: Pointer may be null; caller must check before dereferencing.
Thread-safety relies on holding the associated lock while using the returned pointer.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::operator->
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const T* BT::LockedPtr<T>::operator->() const
functions.description: Const arrow operator returning the stored raw pointer for member access. Intended for read-only access to the protected object while the mutex is held.
requirements: The stored pointer must be non-null before use; otherwise dereferencing via operator-> causes undefined behavior.
Caller is responsible for ensuring the mutex is currently locked when accessing the object.

functions.name: BT::LockedPtr::assign
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
template <typename OtherT>
void BT::LockedPtr<T>::assign(const OtherT& other)
functions.description: Assigns a value to the referenced object. If T and OtherT are the same, performs direct assignment. If OtherT is BT::Any, calls other->copyInto(*ref_). Otherwise attempts to construct T from OtherT. Throws std::runtime_error if no object is referenced.
requirements: ref_ must be non-null; otherwise a std::runtime_error("Empty LockedPtr reference") is thrown.
For direct assignment, T and OtherT must be the same type and T must be assignable.
For BT::Any input, OtherT must be BT::Any and other must support operator-> and provide copyInto(T&) semantics as used in safe_any.hpp.
For conversion assignment, T must be constructible from OtherT (i.e., T(other) must be well-formed).
Caller should hold the associated lock while calling assign() to maintain thread-safety (the function does not lock/unlock internally).

functions.name: BT::WakeUpSignal::waitFor
functions.description: Waits up to the specified timeout for a wake-up signal and returns true if the signal was received before the timeout, otherwise false. Internally uses a condition_variable with a predicate to avoid spurious wake-ups and resets the ready flag to false before returning. Typical usage: call from one or more threads to block until another thread invokes emitSignal(), or until the timeout elapses.
requirements: The usec argument specifies the maximum wait duration; very small or zero durations may cause the function to return immediately if no signal is ready.
This call may block the calling thread until either the signal is received or the timeout expires.
On return, the internal ready flag is reset; subsequent waits will block again until another signal is emitted.

functions.name: BT::WakeUpSignal::emitSignal
functions.description: Emits a wake-up signal that sets the internal ready flag and notifies all waiters on the condition variable. Typical usage: call from a producer or controller thread to wake any threads currently waiting in waitFor(). Multiple waiters are awakened due to notify_all().
requirements: Can be called from any thread; it will wake all threads currently blocked in waitFor().
If no thread is currently waiting, the next waitFor() will observe the ready flag and return immediately, after which the flag is reset by waitFor().

functions.name: BT::Signal::notify
functions.description: Synchronously invokes all currently active subscribers of this Signal with the provided arguments, removing any expired subscribers before continuing. Use to broadcast an event with parameters to all listeners that remain subscribed via a live shared_ptr. Details such as threading and exception handling are not specified in this header.
requirements: All active subscribers must be invocable with the argument types (CallableArgs...) supplied to notify; otherwise undefined behavior or compilation errors may occur.
If any subscriber’s callable throws, notify will not handle it (propagates per normal C++ rules); caller should be prepared for exceptions. (Inferred from direct call of std::function.)
No thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls to notify/subscribe from multiple threads are unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: BT::Signal::subscribe
functions.description: Registers a new subscriber (callable) to be invoked on subsequent notify() calls and returns a shared_ptr handle controlling the subscription’s lifetime. The subscription remains active while at least one copy of the returned shared_ptr exists or until the handle’s reset() is called. Intended for implementing a simple observable pattern.
requirements: func must be a valid (non-empty) std::function target; subscribing an empty std::function will cause a std::bad_function_call when notify() invokes it.
Keep the returned std::shared_ptr alive to remain subscribed; letting it go out of scope or calling reset() will unsubscribe.
The callable’s signature must be exactly void(CallableArgs...), matching the Signal’s template parameters.
No thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls to subscribe/notify are unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: wildcards_match
functions.signature: inline bool wildcards_match(std::string_view str, std::string_view pattern)
functions.description: Matches the input string against a wildcard pattern supporting '*' (matches any sequence, including empty) and '?' (matches any single character). Uses recursion with memoization for efficiency. Typical use: pass the candidate text as str and a pattern possibly containing '*' and '?' as pattern; the function returns true if the entire str matches the entire pattern, otherwise false. Matching is done by exact character comparison for non-wildcard characters; no locale or case folding is applied. The function is pure (no side effects) and may allocate memory for its memoization table.
requirements: str and pattern must reference valid character sequences for the duration of the call (i.e., their underlying data must not be invalidated while the function executes).
Matching is byte-wise on the characters of std::string_view; non-wildcard characters must match exactly; '*' matches any sequence (including empty); '?' matches any single character.
Inputs may be empty; an empty pattern matches only an empty string.

The function allocates a memoization table of size (str.size()+1)*(pattern.size()+1); callers should ensure input sizes are reasonable to avoid excessive memory use or allocation failure (std::bad_alloc).
No special termination or encoding requirements are imposed by the function; it does not read past the views' bounds.
Return value is boolean indicating full-string match; no error codes are returned. Allocation failure may throw std::bad_alloc.

functions.name: BT::AlwaysSuccessNode::AlwaysSuccessNode
functions.description: Constructor for a behavior tree synchronous action node that always returns SUCCESS when ticked. Use this to create a named AlwaysSuccessNode instance; the constructor forwards the name to the SyncActionNode base and sets the node’s registration ID to "AlwaysSuccess". No input/output ports are declared for this node.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid std::string for parameter 'name'.
This node defines no input or output ports (an empty port list is passed to the base class); callers should not expect or rely on ports.
BehaviorTree.CPP runtime must have access to the BT::SyncActionNode base class (i.e., include and linkage) to construct this node.

functions.name: BT::AlwaysFailureNode::AlwaysFailureNode
functions.description: Constructor for a BehaviorTree.CPP synchronous action node that always returns NodeStatus::FAILURE when ticked. Initializes the base SyncActionNode with the provided node name and no ports, and sets the registration ID to "AlwaysFailure". Use to create a leaf that forces failure in a behavior tree (e.g., for testing or control-flow design).
requirements: The caller must provide a valid std::string for the node name (can be empty; no further constraints are specified).
BehaviorTree.CPP headers (behaviortree_cpp/action_node.h) must be available at compile time, and the code must link against the BehaviorTree.CPP library.
The constructed object is intended to be used within the BehaviorTree.CPP framework and ticked by the tree engine; no additional constructor preconditions are specified.

functions.name: BT::ScriptNode::ScriptNode
functions.signature: BT::ScriptNode::ScriptNode(const std::string& name, const BT::NodeConfig& config)
functions.description: Constructs a ScriptNode action node, registers it with ID "ScriptNode", and immediately attempts to parse and compile the script provided through the input port "code" into an executable ScriptFunction. Intended for use within BehaviorTree.CPP trees where this node executes user-provided script code. Notes: the constructor calls an internal loadExecutor() that fetches the "code" input port and parses it right away; missing or invalid code will cause construction to throw.
requirements: config must provide an input port named "code" of type std::string; if missing, the constructor throws a RuntimeError("Missing port [code] in Script").
The value of the "code" port must be syntactically valid for ParseScript; otherwise the constructor throws a RuntimeError containing the parser error message.
The provided NodeConfig should be appropriate for a SyncActionNode (i.e., consistent with BehaviorTree.CPP node construction); otherwise behavior is undefined (library-defined).

functions.name: BT::ScriptNode::providedPorts
functions.description: Returns the list of ports used by ScriptNode. It declares a single input port named "code" of type std::string, described as a piece of code that can be parsed. Used by BehaviorTree.CPP to validate and wire ports when building the tree.
requirements: Call without an instance (static).
Consumers should supply a std::string to the input port "code" when instantiating or configuring this node, as the node requires it during construction and execution.

functions.name: BT::ScriptCondition::ScriptCondition
functions.description: Constructs a ScriptCondition behavior tree node. It registers the node type as "ScriptCondition" and eagerly loads/compiles the script from the "code" input port by invoking loadExecutor(). Intended usage: instantiate via the BehaviorTree factory with the required input port mapping; the node evaluates the provided script at tick-time and returns SUCCESS when the script evaluates to true, FAILURE otherwise. Throws on missing or invalid script during construction.
requirements: config must provide an input port named "code" that can be read at construction time via getInput; otherwise a RuntimeError("Missing port [code] in ScriptCondition") is thrown.
The "code" input must contain a script that can be parsed by ParseScript; if parsing fails, a RuntimeError with the parser error message is thrown.
The script must evaluate to a boolean (true/false) at runtime; non-boolean results will cause a bad cast or undefined behavior when result.cast<bool>() is performed during tick().
The node uses the blackboard and enums from config when executing the script; these should be initialized as needed for the script to run correctly.

functions.name: BT::ScriptCondition::providedPorts
functions.description: Returns the list of ports required by ScriptCondition. It declares a single input port named "code", described as a piece of code that must return true or false. Typical usage: the BehaviorTree factory queries this to know which ports to bind or remap when constructing the node.

functions.signature:

functions.description: Constructor for the deprecated decorator node ConsumeQueue<T>. Initializes the decorator with a node name and configuration. This node repeatedly consumes items from an input queue port and sets an output port with the popped item while ticking its single child. Note: This class is deprecated (use LoopNode instead).
requirements: The node is a decorator and must have exactly one child node configured before execution (standard DecoratorNode contract).

The NodeConfig should be compatible with the ports declared by providedPorts(), i.e., an input port named "queue" of type std::shared_ptr<ProtectedQueue<T>> and an output port named "popped_item" of type T.
Template parameter T must match the element type stored in the provided ProtectedQueue<T> and the type of the "popped_item" output port.

functions.name: BT::ConsumeQueue::tick
functions.description: Ticks the ConsumeQueue<T> decorator. If a valid queue is provided via the "queue" input port, it pops items one by one and, for each popped item, writes it to the "popped_item" output port and ticks the single child. It continues until the queue becomes empty or the child returns RUNNING/FAILURE. If the child is RUNNING, the decorator returns RUNNING and resumes later. If the child returns FAILURE for any item, the decorator returns FAILURE immediately. If no queue is provided or the queue is empty, it returns SUCCESS by default. Deprecated: prefer LoopNode.
requirements: Must be used as a decorator with exactly one child node; the child must be valid and tickable.
If the "queue" input port is set, it must contain a non-null std::shared_ptr<ProtectedQueue<T>> whose mutex (mtx) and item container (items) are valid and usable.
The template parameter T must match the element type of the provided ProtectedQueue<T> and the type expected by the "popped_item" output port.

Callers expecting to consume items must connect the "queue" input port and the "popped_item" output port appropriately; otherwise, the node will simply return SUCCESS when the queue is empty or missing.
Callers should be prepared to handle return statuses: RUNNING while the child is running on a popped item, FAILURE if the child fails for any item, and SUCCESS otherwise.

functions.name: BT::ConsumeQueue::providedPorts
functions.description: Declares the ports used by ConsumeQueue<T>. Exposes an input port named "queue" carrying std::shared_ptr<ProtectedQueue<T>> and an output port named "popped_item" of type T. Use this to configure/validate blackboard connections for this node. Deprecated node; prefer LoopNode.
requirements: None at call-site beyond typical static port declaration usage. Consumers of this API should connect: input port "queue" as std::shared_ptr<ProtectedQueue<T>>, and output port "popped_item" as T.
Template parameter T must be consistent with both the queue element type and the output port type.

functions.name: BT::DelayNode::providedPorts

Callers should expect only BT::NodeStatus::RUNNING or BT::NodeStatus::FAILURE as return values; any completed child status (e.g., SUCCESS or FAILURE) causes this node to return FAILURE after resetting the child.

Intended for use by the BehaviorTree engine during tree execution.
